_initial_state_note: Replaces the old num_incumbent_cohorts warm start (simulated cohorts admitted at negative terms). The university starts NOT empty: 'occupancy' is how many seats in each course are already taken by the existing student body the first simulated cohort competes against -- a steady-state background load subtracted from that course's free seats on every mandatory term (see src/simulator.py::_effective_capacity and CLAUDE.md's Initial-State Model). 'standing' is a rough head-count of existing students at each year-standing, added as a constant to the aggregate stage-flow chart so it starts non-empty. Edit these in Settings or the Scenario Builder. num_incumbent_cohorts still works as an engine knob (defaults to 0 / no incumbents) but is no longer part of the default plan.
_optional_terms_note: Fall and Spring are mandatory (the only seasons that advance a student's personal_semester clock / max_terms budget; see CLAUDE.md's Term/Season Model). Summer is an optional intersession: a course must explicitly list 'Summer' in its own offering array to run then, and gets a smaller capacity than its mandatory-term seats -- optional_term_capacity_scale x course.capacity. The cycle is 3 seasons (Fall, Spring, Summer), so one year = 3 terms and admit_interval_terms=3 keeps yearly Fall-only admissions. In the default QU plan, ONLY the 22 non-CS service courses (math/science/english/gen_ed) are offered in Summer -- CS courses are never offered in Summer, matching QU's real schedule. optional_terms_enabled defaults to TRUE here: Summer is on. Turning it off (Settings -> PUT /config) collapses to the legacy 2-season Fall/Spring cycle; admit_interval_terms then auto-rescales to 2 so Fall-only yearly admission is preserved either way -- see src/models/semester.py::effective_admit_interval_terms. (The engine's season model is fully generic: an admin could define any terms_per_year cycle, e.g. add a Winter intersession, entirely from config -- nothing about the season names is hardcoded; see tests/test_optional_terms.py.)
_registration_tier_note: Seat-priority bands by completed_ch, checked in descending order (registration_tier 0 = registers first). QU's real priority-registration policy; a different institution redefines its own bands here, not in student.py::registration_tier.
_year_standing_note: Ascending completed-CH cutoffs for the flow chart's Year1->Year2->Year3->Year4 stage nodes. QU's actual 4-year/120-CH bands (30 CH/year); a program with a different total credit-hour count sets its own bands here, not in student.py::curriculum_stage.
_on_time_note: Semesters-to-graduate cutoff for the on_time_rate metric (finished at/under this counts as 'on time'). QU's standard 4-year/8-semester schedule; a program with a different standard length sets its own value here, not in analytics.py.
_enrollment_priority_note: Phase-1 desired-enrollment order, tried after retakes (which always come first and are not part of this list). Each tier is {categories: [...], min_ch?: N}; a student's eligible courses are bucketed into the first tier whose categories contains the course's category AND whose min_ch (default 0) the student's completed_ch already meets, then tiers are filled in order up to the load cap. A category absent from every tier, or gated by an unmet min_ch, is simply not enrolled that term. This is QU CS's policy (required courses, then cs_electives once junior-standing CH is reached, then service/gen-ed courses) expressed as data; a different program redefines its own tiers/categories here, not in student.py.
_dropout_note: Dropout has three causes. PRIMARY (GPA): each term a student with completed_ch >= probation_min_ch and gpa < dropout_gpa_floor leaves with probability base_hazard*(1+(floor-gpa)), doubled (early_multiplier) in their first dropout_early_sem_cutoff semesters. SECONDARY (gateway): failing one course dropout_fails_threshold times drops them with prob dropout_prob_on_repeated_fail. TERTIARY (cumulative delay, opt-in via dropout_delay_hazard_scale, default 0.0 = off): independent of GPA, a student whose completed_ch has fallen behind the pace implied by on_time_terms faces a per-term hazard of dropout_delay_hazard_scale * (credit-hour deficit / total program CH) -- models real students who withdraw once they've fallen far enough behind, rather than passively riding it out to CENSORED at the horizon. Left at 0.0 by default; an admin can opt in per plan. CALIBRATION SCOPE: base_hazard is tuned so aggregate 12-semester graduation lands near the middle of a plausible 50-70% range for a program this length — an internally-chosen target, not fit to external data. The early_multiplier front-loading is a face-validity assumption, not a data fit. UPDATE (post optional-term model): a 30-seed sweep of base_hazard over 0.15-0.21 now moves graduation by 0.78pp (0.7382 -> 0.7304) with dropout/censored moving in opposite directions -- a real, monotone relationship, not the flat dropped<->censored trade found before optional terms existed. This swing is now LARGER than the gateway-capacity sweep's ~0.1pp (see _sections_note) -- the reverse of the original ranking. See docs/project_overview.md for how dropout/GPA mechanics work.
